content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

## Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

## Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

## Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

## Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
", "id": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

{"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1759288987.503349", "type": "message", "text": "We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it’s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

content.text: I'll write a small helper to decode thread bodies from saved files.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/dec.py <<'EOF'
import json,sys,base64
d=json.loads(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))['result'])
msgs=d['messages'] if 'messages' in d else [d]
def walk(p):
    out=[]
    if p.get('mimeType','').startswith('text/plain') and p.get('body',{}).get('data'):
        out.append(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p['body']['data']+'==').decode('utf-8','replace'))
    for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []: out+=walk(c)
    return out
lim=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 3000
for m in msgs:
    h={x['name']:x['value'] for x in m['payload']['headers']}
    print('=====',h.get('Date'),'|',h.get('From'),'->',h.get('To'),'| cc',h.get('Cc'),'|',h.get('Subject'))
    t='\n'.join(walk(m['payload']))
    # strip quoted
    lines=[l for l in t.split('\n') if not l.startswith('>')]
    print('\n'.join(lines)[:lim])
EOF

TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. You\\u2019re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We\\u2019ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we\\u2019d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.\\n\\nThanks again for sharing the journey with us. {"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1759288987.503349", "type": "message", "text": "We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it’s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

At the center is Harmony Games Engine—our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the “live service” layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. Intro Slide
 Hi There, and thank you for taking the time today. Slide: The Company
 I am Leonard, co-founder and CEO of Harmony Games, joined by my co-founders [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake and a senior team across product, UA, analytics, Unity, backend, and art. We founded the company in 2023, raised a 3 million dollar seed, and built a lean 17 to 20 person core team operating across the United States, Turkey, Eastern Europe, and South America with low-cost development partners. Our mission is simple and disciplined: rapidly build and test breakthrough mechanics, then scale the winners on a reusable, AI-assisted engine so creativity becomes a defensible advantage rather than a one-off. Our vision is to build the world’s best puzzle RPGs with Turkish execution DNA and global scale.
Slide: Market
 Puzzle RPG is a 1.2 billion dollar mobile category that is ripe for disruption. Eastern titles prove the ceiling while Western match-3 plus RPG clones show fatigue, and the contenders that break out do so with fresh core experiences rather than more of the same. Our thesis is to carve out a Western-first, mechanic-first blue ocean and build the next 100 million dollar puzzle RPG franchise.
Slide: The Harmony Games Engine
 We are not just building games. We are building systems that shorten time to proof and let us reuse success. Version 1.0 of the Harmony Games Engine took roughly 15 months to build. We are now porting those systems into new titles in about four months with production-level quality and full LiveOps integration. The platform spans LiveOps automation, advanced leaderboards, seasonal content, team and social systems, dynamic difficulty, AI-assisted level creation with smart bots, and a flexible 3D puzzle layer with physics and expandable boosters. This is why we can move from concept to soft launch on a single green-light cycle and operate with a small, fast team.
Slide: Engine Demos
 In the meeting, we will show brief clips of the Puzzle Engine and the LiveOps Engine to highlight how content, economy events, and leaderboards are configured without heavy engineering. The important takeaway is that net-new code is minimized while speed and reliability are maximized.
Slide: Pragmatic Marketing AI
 Our user acquisition approach is tool-first, not platform-first. Creative is king in mobile UA, so our pipeline focuses on throughput: concept to first testable video in about two hours, with weekly rotations and hard kills on weak lines. We are already producing playables because networks increasingly favor short interactive ads, and we use best-in-class tools to accelerate hook testing, copy, VO, and assembly without bloating the team.
Slide: Studio Roadmap
 Our cadence is something investors can model. We standardized LiveOps Engine v1.0 and shipped Puzzle Engine v1.0 with an AI co-pilot for level creation. We are iterating toward LiveOps v2.0 for personalization and Puzzle Engine v2.0 for adaptive or auto-generated levels. On this spine, we progress titles in parallel and target a new live beta roughly every four to five months, culminating in Zombie Match 3D global timing on the roadmap.
Slide: Domino Delights
 Domino Delights was our proving ground. We validated the production content pipeline, physics, boosters, effects, events, leaderboards, A/B testing, shop and offers, analytics hygiene, and localization plus build operations. We deliberately de-scoped heavy narrative, UA scale, and long-tail tuning because the goal was to harden the engine, not to over-invest before we had proof.
Slide: LiveOps Event Library
 Retention is a calendar, so we invested early in an expanding LiveOps library. We support single-player events like win-and-collect and unique modes, PvP-style fastest-completion and usage leaderboards, daily and weekly quests, login calendars, season pass and trophy paths, and team systems with GvG underway. These are authorable systems that let us ship frequent, reliable engagement beats from day one.
Slide: Decision Discipline
 Our Turkish DNA is to test, kill, and scale with honesty. Domino Delights creatives and CPI tested well and D1 in the low to mid 40s was encouraging, but D7 settled around the mid teens with a roughly 35 percent D7 to D1 ratio, which capped LTV against CPI outside small budgets. We stopped scaling, shipped the learnings, and pivoted quickly to a better core engagement mechanic while reusing the stack. That discipline unlocked a four-month port to our next title.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Overview
 Zombie Match 3D is our wedge for Western audiences. The core is rapid-fire 3D “match and slash” where every matched object becomes a weapon, layered with an item arsenal and upgrades for deeper monetization, plus bosses and horde modes for session variety. LiveOps is built in from day one so we can operate like a service, not a demo.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Progress
 We have a zombie and UI overhaul in progress for beta, and the item upgrade system is built with effects like shockwave, poison, and stun to drive satisfying power curves without harming accessibility. The result is a loop that reads fast and fun while opening room for event-driven depth.
Slide: Zombie LiveOps Status
 LiveOps integration in Zombie Match sits at roughly 60 percent complete with the remaining 40 percent landing on a short horizon. Trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, and teams are online or in final integration, which means we can move into soft-launch operations with confidence in cadence and tooling.
Slide: Alpha Signals and Near-Term Gates
 Early UK iOS alpha with roughly 300 installs showed D1 around 34 percent, day-zero playtime around 23 minutes, and CPI around 4.5 dollars at minimal polish. Over the next six to eight weeks, we expand content to 500 plus levels, complete the polish and VFX pass, and scale UA to two to three thousand users for stable reads. Our gates are explicit: D1 at least 45 percent, D7 to D1 at least 45 percent, and CPI at or below 3.50 dollars in UK iOS tests. We scale only if the data clears the gates.
Slide: The Raise and Use of Proceeds
 We are raising a 2.5 million dollar bridge that extends runway to 18 months or more. The use of funds is approximately 1.5 million dollars for product and engine and 1.0 million dollars for soft-launch UA. The milestones to unlock the next round before worldwide launch include D1 in the mid to high 40s, D7 in the low to mid 20s, CPI targets by geo and platform, early payer rates, and 60 to 90 day ROAS gates.
Slide: Why Harmony Games
 We believe Harmony Games is an efficient bet on the next breakout in puzzle RPG for three reasons. First, we are platform-first, with modular, AI-assisted systems for puzzle generation, LiveOps, analytics, and UA that are already production-Proven and let us ship a content-ready beta in four to five months once the core game is Proven. Second, we operate with Turkish model discipline: test, kill, and scale, with low burn around 100 thousand dollars per month and clear decision gates that keep CAC and LTV honest, which is uncommon among Western teams. Third, we have a distinct genre wedge with Match and Slash that pairs broad Western appeal and 3D visual punch with RPG monetization depth, positioned to stand out amid look-alikes.

\"1756943018.637589\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Below are VC-ready speaker notes in full sentences, aligned to your \\u201cHarmony Games Pitch\\u201d deck and formatted exactly like your Use them verbatim or as a talk track.\\nIntro Slide\\n Hi There, and thank you for taking the time today. We would love to walk you through Harmony Games, show how our platform approach de-risks the hit-making process in puzzle RPG, and share what we are building now. Please jump in with candid feedback, and if this resonates, we would be excited to continue the conversation after this meeting.\\nSlide: The Company\\n I am Leonard, co-founder and CEO of Harmony Games, joined by my co-founders [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake and a senior team across product, UA, analytics, Unity, backend, and art. We founded the company in 2023, raised a 3 million dollar seed, and built a lean 17 to 20 person core team operating across the United States, Turkey, Eastern Europe, and South America with low-cost development partners. Our mission is simple and disciplined: rapidly build and test breakthrough mechanics, then scale the winners on a reusable, AI-assisted engine so creativity becomes a defensible advantage rather than a one-off. Our vision is to build the world\\u2019s best puzzle RPGs with Turkish execution DNA and global scale.\\nSlide: Market\\n Puzzle RPG is a 1.2 billion dollar mobile category that is ripe for disruption. Eastern titles prove the ceiling while Western match-3 plus RPG clones show fatigue, and the contenders that break out do so with fresh core experiences rather than more of the same. Our thesis is to carve out a Western-first, mechanic-first blue ocean and build the next 100 million dollar puzzle RPG franchise.\\nSlide: The Harmony Games Engine\\n We are not just building games. We are building systems that shorten time to proof and let us reuse success. Version 1.0 of the Harmony Games Engine took roughly 15 months to build. We are now porting those systems into new titles in about four months with production-level quality and full LiveOps integration. The platform spans LiveOps automation, advanced leaderboards, seasonal content, team and social systems, dynamic difficulty, AI-assisted level creation with smart bots, and a flexible 3D puzzle layer with physics and expandable boosters. This is why we can move from concept to soft launch on a single green-light cycle and operate with a small, fast team.\\nSlide: Engine Demos\\n In the meeting, we will show brief clips of the Puzzle Engine and the LiveOps Engine to highlight how content, economy events, and leaderboards are configured without heavy engineering. The important takeaway is that net-new code is minimized while speed and reliability are maximized.\\nSlide: Pragmatic Marketing AI\\n Our user acquisition approach is tool-first, not platform-first. Creative is king in mobile UA, so our pipeline focuses on throughput: concept to first testable video in about two hours, with weekly rotations and hard kills on weak lines. We are already producing playables because networks increasingly favor short interactive ads, and we use best-in-class tools to accelerate hook testing, copy, VO, and assembly without bloating the team.\\nSlide: Studio Roadmap\\n Our cadence is something investors can model. We standardized LiveOps Engine v1.0 and shipped Puzzle Engine v1.0 with an AI co-pilot for level creation. We are iterating toward LiveOps v2.0 for personalization and Puzzle Engine v2.0 for adaptive or auto-generated levels. On this spine, we progress titles in parallel and target a new live beta roughly every four to five months, culminating in Zombie Match 3D global timing on the roadmap.\\nSlide: Domino Delights\\n Domino Delights was our proving ground. We validated the production content pipeline, physics, boosters, effects, events, leaderboards, A/B testing, shop and offers, analytics hygiene, and localization plus build operations. We deliberately de-scoped heavy narrative, UA scale, and long-tail tuning because the goal was to harden the engine, not to over-invest before we had proof.\\nSlide: LiveOps Event Library\\n Retention is a calendar, so we invested early in an expanding LiveOps library. We support single-player events like win-and-collect and unique modes, PvP-style fastest-completion and usage leaderboards, daily and weekly quests, login calendars, season pass and trophy paths, and team systems with GvG underway. These are authorable systems that let us ship frequent, reliable engagement beats from day one.\\nSlide: Decision Discipline\\n Our Turkish DNA is to test, kill, and scale with honesty. Domino Delights creatives and CPI tested well and D1 in the low to mid 40s was encouraging, but D7 settled around the mid teens with a roughly 35 percent D7 to D1 ratio, which capped LTV against CPI outside small budgets. We stopped scaling, shipped the learnings, and pivoted quickly to a better core engagement mechanic while reusing the stack. That discipline unlocked a four-month port to our next title.\\nSlide: Zombie Match 3D Overview\\n Zombie Match 3D is our wedge for Western audiences. The core is rapid-fire 3D \\u201cmatch and slash\\u201d where every matched object becomes a weapon, layered with an item arsenal and upgrades for deeper monetization, plus bosses and horde modes for session variety. LiveOps is built in from day one so we can operate like a service, not a demo.\\nSlide: Zombie Match 3D Progress\\n We have a zombie and UI overhaul in progress for beta, and the item upgrade system is built with effects like shockwave, poison, and stun to drive satisfying power curves without harming accessibility. The result is a loop that reads fast and fun while opening room for event-driven depth.\\nSlide: Zombie LiveOps Status\\n LiveOps integration in Zombie Match sits at roughly 60 percent complete with the remaining 40 percent landing on a short horizon. Trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, and teams are online or in final integration, which means we can move into soft-launch operations with confidence in cadence and tooling.\\nSlide: Alpha Signals and Near-Term Gates\\n Early UK iOS alpha with roughly 300 installs showed D1 around 34 percent, day-zero playtime around 23 minutes, and CPI around 4.5 dollars at minimal polish. Over the next six to eight weeks, we expand content to 500 plus levels, complete the polish and VFX pass, and scale UA to two to three thousand users for stable reads. Our gates are explicit: D1 at least 45 percent, D7 to D1 at least 45 percent, and CPI at or below 3.50 dollars in UK iOS tests. We scale only if the data clears the gates.\\nSlide: The Raise and Use of Proceeds\\n We are raising a 2.5 million dollar bridge that extends runway to 18 months or more. The use of funds is approximately 1.5 million dollars for product and engine and 1.0 million dollars for soft-launch UA. The milestones to unlock the next round before worldwide launch include D1 in the mid to high 40s, D7 in the low to mid 20s, CPI targets by geo and platform, early payer rates, and 60 to 90 day ROAS gates.\\nSlide: Why Harmony Games\\n We believe Harmony Games is an efficient bet on the next breakout in puzzle RPG for three reasons. First, we are platform-first, with modular, AI-assisted systems for puzzle generation, LiveOps, analytics, and UA that are already production-Proven and let us ship a content-ready beta in four to five months once the core game is Proven. Second, we operate with Turkish model discipline: test, kill, and scale, with low burn around 100 thousand dollars per month and clear decision gates that keep CAC and LTV honest, which is uncommon among Western teams. Third, we have a distinct genre wedge with Match and Slash that pairs broad Western appeal and 3D visual punch with RPG monetization depth, positioned to stand out amid look-alikes.\\nClosing Slide\\n Thank you again for your time. We welcome questions on the platform, the roadmap, and the data behind our gates, and we would be glad to dive deeper into the Zombie Match 3D soft-launch plan and the LiveOps v2.0 feature set. "1756943018.637589", "type": "message", "text": "Below are VC-ready speaker notes in full sentences, aligned to your “Harmony Games Pitch” deck and formatted exactly like your example. Use them verbatim or as a talk track.
Intro Slide
 Hi There, and thank you for taking the time today. We would love to walk you through Harmony Games, show how our platform approach de-risks the hit-making process in puzzle RPG, and share what we are building now. Please jump in with candid feedback, and if this resonates, we would be excited to continue the conversation after this meeting.
Slide: The Company
 I am Leonard, co-founder and CEO of Harmony Games, joined by my co-founders [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake and a senior team across product, UA, analytics, Unity, backend, and art. We founded the company in 2023, raised a 3 million dollar seed, and built a lean 17 to 20 person core team operating across the United States, Turkey, Eastern Europe, and South America with low-cost development partners. Our mission is simple and disciplined: rapidly build and test breakthrough mechanics, then scale the winners on a reusable, AI-assisted engine so creativity becomes a defensible advantage rather than a one-off. Our vision is to build the world’s best puzzle RPGs with Turkish execution DNA and global scale.
Slide: Market
 Puzzle RPG is a 1.2 billion dollar mobile category that is ripe for disruption. Eastern titles prove the ceiling while Western match-3 plus RPG clones show fatigue, and the contenders that break out do so with fresh core experiences rather than more of the same. Our thesis is to carve out a Western-first, mechanic-first blue ocean and build the next 100 million dollar puzzle RPG franchise.
Slide: The Harmony Games Engine
 We are not just building games. We are building systems that shorten time to proof and let us reuse success. Version 1.0 of the Harmony Games Engine took roughly 15 months to build. We are now porting those systems into new titles in about four months with production-level quality and full LiveOps integration. The platform spans LiveOps automation, advanced leaderboards, seasonal content, team and social systems, dynamic difficulty, AI-assisted level creation with smart bots, and a flexible 3D puzzle layer with physics and expandable boosters. This is why we can move from concept to soft launch on a single green-light cycle and operate with a small, fast team.
Slide: Engine Demos
 In the meeting, we will show brief clips of the Puzzle Engine and the LiveOps Engine to highlight how content, economy events, and leaderboards are configured without heavy engineering. The important takeaway is that net-new code is minimized while speed and reliability are maximized.
Slide: Pragmatic Marketing AI
 Our user acquisition approach is tool-first, not platform-first. Creative is king in mobile UA, so our pipeline focuses on throughput: concept to first testable video in about two hours, with weekly rotations and hard kills on weak lines. We are already producing playables because networks increasingly favor short interactive ads, and we use best-in-class tools to accelerate hook testing, copy, VO, and assembly without bloating the team.
Slide: Studio Roadmap
 Our cadence is something investors can model. We standardized LiveOps Engine v1.0 and shipped Puzzle Engine v1.0 with an AI co-pilot for level creation. We are iterating toward LiveOps v2.0 for personalization and Puzzle Engine v2.0 for adaptive or auto-generated levels. On this spine, we progress titles in parallel and target a new live beta roughly every four to five months, culminating in Zombie Match 3D global timing on the roadmap.
Slide: Domino Delights
 Domino Delights was our proving ground. We validated the production content pipeline, physics, boosters, effects, events, leaderboards, A/B testing, shop and offers, analytics hygiene, and localization plus build operations. We deliberately de-scoped heavy narrative, UA scale, and long-tail tuning because the goal was to harden the engine, not to over-invest before we had proof.
Slide: LiveOps Event Library
 Retention is a calendar, so we invested early in an expanding LiveOps library. We support single-player events like win-and-collect and unique modes, PvP-style fastest-completion and usage leaderboards, daily and weekly quests, login calendars, season pass and trophy paths, and team systems with GvG underway. These are authorable systems that let us ship frequent, reliable engagement beats from day one.
Slide: Decision Discipline
 Our Turkish DNA is to test, kill, and scale with honesty. Domino Delights creatives and CPI tested well and D1 in the low to mid 40s was encouraging, but D7 settled around the mid teens with a roughly 35 percent D7 to D1 ratio, which capped LTV against CPI outside small budgets. We stopped scaling, shipped the learnings, and pivoted quickly to a better core engagement mechanic while reusing the stack. That discipline unlocked a four-month port to our next title.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Overview
 Zombie Match 3D is our wedge for Western audiences. The core is rapid-fire 3D “match and slash” where every matched object becomes a weapon, layered with an item arsenal and upgrades for deeper monetization, plus bosses and horde modes for session variety. LiveOps is built in from day one so we can operate like a service, not a demo.
Slide: Zombie Match 3D Progress
 We have a zombie and UI overhaul in progress for beta, and the item upgrade system is built with effects like shockwave, poison, and stun to drive satisfying power curves without harming accessibility. The result is a loop that reads fast and fun while opening room for event-driven depth.
Slide: Zombie LiveOps Status
 LiveOps integration in Zombie Match sits at roughly 60 percent complete with the remaining 40 percent landing on a short horizon. Trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, and teams are online or in final integration, which means we can move into soft-launch operations with confidence in cadence and tooling.
Slide: Alpha Signals and Near-Term Gates
 Early UK iOS alpha with roughly 300 installs showed D1 around 34 percent, day-zero playtime around 23 minutes, and CPI around 4.5 dollars at minimal polish. Over the next six to eight weeks, we expand content to 500 plus levels, complete the polish and VFX pass, and scale UA to two to three thousand users for stable reads. Our gates are explicit: D1 at least 45 percent, D7 to D1 at least 45 percent, and CPI at or below 3.50 dollars in UK iOS tests. We scale only if the data clears the gates.
Slide: The Raise and Use of Proceeds
 We are raising a 2.5 million dollar bridge that extends runway to 18 months or more. The use of funds is approximately 1.5 million dollars for product and engine and 1.0 million dollars for soft-launch UA. The milestones to unlock the next round before worldwide launch include D1 in the mid to high 40s, D7 in the low to mid 20s, CPI targets by geo and platform, early payer rates, and 60 to 90 day ROAS gates.
Slide: Why Harmony Games
 We believe Harmony Games is an efficient bet on the next breakout in puzzle RPG for three reasons. First, we are platform-first, with modular, AI-assisted systems for puzzle generation, LiveOps, analytics, and UA that are already production-Proven and let us ship a content-ready beta in four to five months once the core game is Proven. Second, we operate with Turkish model discipline: test, kill, and scale, with low burn around 100 thousand dollars per month and clear decision gates that keep CAC and LTV honest, which is uncommon among Western teams. Third, we have a distinct genre wedge with Match and Slash that pairs broad Western appeal and 3D visual punch with RPG monetization depth, positioned to stand out amid look-alikes.
Closing Slide
 Thank you again for your time. We welcome questions on the platform, the roadmap, and the data behind our gates, and we would be glad to dive deeper into the Zombie Match 3D soft-launch plan and the LiveOps v2.0 feature set. Leonard,

Done. "Q4 update - send list" is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with you. Groups are as of end of day Sep 30 PT, following your doc:

- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $40K. His DocuSign Completed notice came in Sep 26)
- In talks: 7 firms, 0 angels (NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, a16z, GFR, Homa, Brightwater Games Fund)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 3 firms (LVP, Hiro, SciPlay)

That's 25 recipients in total.

A few calls you may want to check on Monday:
- Paul Heydon is off. He told you on Sep 30 that he's out, and we never had a call with him, so he isn't Keep warm either.
- a16z is In talks. The speedrun no is the program's decision, not an answer on the bridge.

NCsoft already had one (the Anel card), so I commented there instead. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) didn't get cards because they already have meetings booked.

Fred

All three of Leonard's asks are done, well before Monday's review: the send list is in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, the Trello card is updated, and I've replied on his thread with the counts. The list has 25 people, with groups as of end of day Sep 30 (Pacific), per his send list doc.

**Counts (what I sent Leonard):**

| Group | Firms | Angels | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 | Anton Bernstein, $40K. His DocuSign "Completed" notice came in Sep 26. |
| In talks | 7 | 0 | NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, a16z, GFR Fund, Homa, Brightwater Games Fund |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 | Makers, Raine, BBQ, General Catalyst, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Treo VC, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital |
| Keep warm | 3 | 0 | LVP, Hiro Capital, SciPlay |

**What I did:**
- **Sheet:** "Q4 update - send list" (the name his README asks for), shared with Leonard as an editor. It has one row each, with group, amount and build access.
- **Trello:** I added four checklists to the Existing Investor Update card, one per group, with an item per firm or angel. I also created 18 "F/up with…" cards in To Do.
  - NCsoft already had a To Do card (the Anel one), so I commented there instead of adding a duplicate.
  - Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) didn't get cards because they already have meetings on your calendar.
- **Reply:** I used reply-all, but it only went to Leonard; Robert and Arthur weren't copied. Forward it to them if they should see it.

**Calls Leonard may question on Monday:**
- **Paul Heydon is off the list.** He told Leonard on Sep 30 that he's out after all, and we never had a call with him, so he doesn't qualify for Keep warm. The Bridge angels sheet still shows him as "in", so it's out of date.
- **a16z is In talks.** Their rejection was for the speedrun program, which his doc says isn't their answer on the bridge.
- **SciPlay is Keep warm.** They passed by phone on Sep 30, after the Sep 15 call; the only record is a Slack thread reply.
- **Play Ventures is off.** They told Griffin no, which his doc counts as a no, and we never had a call with them.
- **Treo VC is Awaiting reply.** They came to us, but Leonard sent them the deck on Sep 3, which I counted as our outreach.
- **Triptyq, Turkven and Harlem are Awaiting reply.** The list only says "IH to reach out", but #bridge-pitch confirms IH did contact them on Sep 12.
- **Build access:** only T-Accelerate and Dentsu are on TestFlight, so both are marked iOS only. Android doesn't work for any investor yet: Arthur found the Play tester list was never attached to the internal test track, and he's fixing it today. The other five firms in talks are marked "none".

Files are in My Drive > … > Q4 2025 investor update:
- Q4 update - send list
